scenarios.inputs: cadence in {20,30,40,60,72,90,110,120} rpm, torque=28 Nm, torque_ripple=45%, asymmetry=8%, mode_type=1
scenarios.proposed_threshold: See comparison_criteria_r3.json (relative_ripple_delta, low_cadence_carveout). Current baseline observation (results/ap01-metrics.json, corrected 3.0-8.0s window): relative_ripple falls monotonically as cadence rises - cad20=0.261, cad30=0.193, cad40=0.165, cad60=0.116, cad72=0.097, cad90=0.077, cad110=0.059, cad120=0.053. CORRECTED interpretation (AP01-R6: the V1 text had this backwards): a fixed-duration observation window contains FEWER completed crank revolutions at low cadence, so the RUN averaging window (assist_torque_run_window_deg, angle-based) completes fewer cycles per second of wall-clock observation - not more - which is consistent with higher residual ripple at low cadence. No numeric tolerance approved yet.

See comparison_criteria_r3.json (relative_ripple_delta). Baseline observation: relative_ripple increases monotonically with asymmetry_pct - asym0=0.091, asym8=0.097, asym30=0.154, asym60=0.252. No accepted max-ripple tolerance yet.

scenarios.inputs: torque or torque_ripple changes value mid-run while PAS stays active (e.g. step from 15 Nm to 40 Nm at t=4s)
metrics: overshoot (max value beyond new steady mean)
scenarios.existing_coverage: tests/host/fw141_torque_elapsed_time_host.c proves the torque filter's elapsed-time model in isolation - see tool_inventory_r4.json for exactly what it does and does not close.
scenarios.extension_needed: lab_cfg_t (controller_lab.c) currently takes a single scalar torque_nm/torque_ripple_pct for the whole run (see controller_lab.c parse_arg, key=value CLI - NOT --flag style). Proposal: add optional step_at_s=<float>, step_torque_nm=<float>, step_torque_ripple_pct=<float> keys, applied additively at generation time only inside the existing synthetic-sensor section, with no change to production torque_input.c/assist_modes.c. Concrete file: motor-controller-firmware/sim/controller_lab/controller_lab.c. Not implemented this rework (no assignment for shared-harness edits; AP01-R4 requires the tool inventory below before any such change is considered).

scenarios.inputs: torque decreases mid-run while PAS stays active (mirror of load_step_during_pas)
pedal, ride_stop_s at t=5, then pedal again (ride_restart_s) before release_ms has fully elapsed
scenarios.existing_coverage: tests/host/fw112_2_rolling_coast_host.c test_s3_coast_resume_no_cold_gate and tests/host/ride_control_rearm_host.c already exhaustively prove the SESSION-STATE correctness of a restart before a coast/release completes - see tool_inventory_r4.json for what remains uncovered (an Iq time-series metric, not a correctness gap).
scenarios.extension_needed: lab_cfg_t has only ONE ride_start_s/ride_stop_s pair (controller_lab.c: 'ride_stop_s <= 0 means never stop', single event). Proposal: extend to an ordered list of (start_s, stop_s) pedalling intervals via repeated ride_start2_s=/ride_stop2_s= keys (key=value, consistent with the existing parser), or a second ride_restart_s= field. Concrete file: same controller_lab.c parse_arg/lab_cfg_t. Not implemented this rework.

scenarios.inputs: speed_kph stays nonzero (freewheeling/rolling) through a stop/restart of pedalling
scenarios.existing_coverage: tests/host/fw112_2_rolling_coast_host.c test_s2/s13/s14 - exhaustive session-state proof of rolling coast/resume/rocking. See tool_inventory_r4.json.
scenarios.extension_needed: same restart-interval extension as stop_then_restart_before_release_complete; speed_kph is already a constant CLI arg independent of ride_start_s/stop_s, so only the restart event itself is missing.

scenarios.inputs: occasional missed 4kHz foreground ticks or PAS-edge jitter
scenarios.existing_coverage: tests/host/fw141_torque_elapsed_time_host.c (call-density invariance) and tests/host/fw137_erps_edge_age_host.c (missing Hall edge decay) are the closest existing proxies; neither exercises an actually-skipped 4kHz tick through the full assist chain. This is the LEAST-covered of the 7 categories - see tool_inventory_r4.json.
scenarios.extension_needed: controller_lab.c drives a fixed CTRL_HZ=4000 loop with no tick-skip injection. Proposal: add a miss_tick_every_n=<int> key (key=value, not --flag) that skips calling the production foreground step function on selected ticks. Needs a Master design decision on which clock the skip applies to (host outer loop vs synthetic sensor only - see tool_inventory_r4.json cross_cutting_note) before any implementation.

scenarios.inputs: crank direction reverses mid-ride (true reverse per FW139 PAS direction safety)
metrics: time to assist inhibit after reverse onset
scenarios.existing_coverage: tests/host/pas_direction_host.c exhaustively proves (797,160 sequences) that reverse/invalid immediately inhibits assist at the unit level; tests/host/fw112_2_rolling_coast_host.c test_s4/s7 confirm it at the session-integration level. The safety property itself is NOT an open gap - only an Iq CSV time-series metric is. See tool_inventory_r4.json.
scenarios.extension_needed: controller_lab.c generates only forward crank_rev progression. Proposal: add reverse_at_s=<float> key flipping the sign of the crank angle rate from that time. Must be reviewed against motor-controller-firmware/AGENTS.md FW139 note so the new synthetic generator does not mask or duplicate pas_direction.c's own safety logic. Not implemented this rework.

scenarios.inputs: torque_sensor_valid / pas_sensor_valid forced false for a window
scenarios.existing_coverage: tests/host/pas_direction_host.c exhaustively covers PAS-decode invalidity. NO existing test was found that forces torque_input.c's torque_sensor_valid specifically - that half of this category is a genuinely new gap, not just a CLI limitation. See tool_inventory_r4.json.
scenarios.extension_needed: controller_lab.c hardcodes r.torque_sensor_valid=true; r.pas_sensor_valid=true unconditionally. Proposal: add torque_invalid_from_s=/torque_invalid_to_s= (and the PAS equivalents) key=value CLI args toggling those two fields inside the existing synthetic-observation struct only. Not implemented this rework.

scenarios.inputs: cadence=72, ride_start_s=0.5, ride_stop_s=5.0 (single stop, the ONE event type the current harness supports)
metrics: stop_points: status, value_at_stop, confirmed_zero_time_s, time_to_confirmed_zero_s, sample_dt_s
scenarios.proposed_threshold: See comparison_criteria_r3.json (S1_stop_latency_ceiling - a CEILING, not a symmetric delta: a shorter stop is not a failure). Observation under the REV3 measurement contract (zero_tolerance=1.0 count, min_confirm_s=0.10 s, max_transition_gap_s=0.05 s): status=CONFIRMED, confirmed_zero_time_s=5.200 s, time_to_confirmed_zero_s=0.200 s, transition bracket [5.195, 5.200] s (one 5 ms sample - this bracket is the uncertainty of the instant, NOT a median sampling interval), observed hold 4.8 s. The V1 figure 0.195 s was the last nonzero sample, not a confirmed settling. Not compared against any accepted release-time contract.

scenarios.inputs: cadence=72, assist_torque_run_window_deg in {30,180,360}, floor vs profile (assist_min_iq_pct=25 vs max_iq_pct=1), without_rotation on/off
metrics: identical-rows comparison against baseline window (audit convention)
per-stage limit evidence over the three observed Iq-chain stages (see comparison_criteria_r3.json L1)
scenarios.result_file: results/window30_repro.csv, window180_repro.csv, window360_repro.csv, floor_above_profile_repro.csv, floor_default_profile1_repro.csv, without_rotation_repro.csv, without_rotation_off_repro.csv
scenarios.proposed_threshold: REPRODUCED audit finding: window30/180/360 rows identical for the tested tuning (window30_vs_180=true, window180_vs_360=true in results/ap01-results.json), consistent with source-manifest.json/probe-results.json prior finding. CORRECTED limit labels (AP01-V3-01), now read STAGE BY STAGE from the three adjacent channel pairs the export provides, instead of one guessed cause: BOTH floor cases show the same two-stage story - profile_limit REDUCED 129-179 -> 7, then post_mode_request RAISED 7 -> 14 (floor 2%) or 7 -> 175 (floor 25%). The REV3 label 'CAP_BINDING 174 -> 14' for the first case was wrong on three counts: it skipped the iq_mode_request stage where the profile limit actually acts, it quoted a single row's 174 as if it were the whole window (the real pre-limit range is 129-179), and it hid the limit-ordering finding that both cases are cut to 7 and then raised above that limit. without_rotation_repro shows profile_limit UNCHANGED (285 -> 285) and post_mode_request REDUCED (285 -> 0), so it is not cap limiting either; without_rotation_off_repro is ZERO_NO_ASSIST. The cause of the post_mode_request stage is deliberately NOT attributed to floor or gate - these two columns do not carry that evidence. No new threshold proposed; this is a determinism/reuse check.
